ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About Snorkel

Snorkel AI is the frontier AI data lab, helping teams build the data and environments behind high-performing frontier and agentic AI. We combine technology with research-driven AI data development to create datasets, benchmarks, evals, and custom solutions for real-world AI systems. Founded out of the Stanford AI Lab in 2019, Snorkel works with leading AI labs and enterprises to move from better data to better outcomes. 

Excited to help us redefine how AI is built? Apply to be the newest Snorkeler!

About Open Benchmarks Grants

Open Benchmarks Grants is Snorkel’s $30M commitment to fund and support researchers and independent builders developing new AI evaluations. We support the teams behind Terminal-Bench, OSWorld 2.0, and Senior SWE-bench, and run a Research Fellows program for PhD students and postdocs. The program funds work in areas including physical AI, scientific discovery, cybersecurity, safety, and alignment, and helps teams test and strengthen their benchmarks before and after public release.

About the Role

Snorkel AI is hiring researchers to support the Open Benchmarks Red Team program.

Frontier AI benchmarks can contain grading failures, exploitable shortcuts, and task errors that make results unreliable. We’re looking for a Research Scientist / Research Engineer to identify benchmark weaknesses, help develop and validate fixes, and create reusable methods to improve benchmark quality across tasks and datasets.

This is a hands-on research role combining AI evaluation, adversarial testing, practical benchmark repairs, and close collaboration with benchmark authors. You'll share findings with benchmark authors, work together on fixes, and help get improved benchmark versions adopted.

What You'll Do

  • Red-team frontier benchmarks: Identify and reproduce issues such as reward hacking, grader failures, task ambiguity, shortcuts, and environment vulnerabilities.
  • Develop benchmark repairs: Propose next steps for validated issues, implement selected fixes with benchmark authors, and verify fixes without breaking valid solutions.
  • Develop reusable methods: Reuse existing tools where possible and develop new checks to detect recurring benchmark weaknesses.
  • Collaborate with benchmark authors: Review findings with benchmark authors before publication, collaborate on repairs, and support official improved releases.
  • Drive research impact: Contribute to technical reports, open-source tools, publications, and new approaches to benchmark evaluation and improvement.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong research or engineering background in machine learning, LLMs, AI agents, and evaluation.
  • Strong Python programming skills and experience building, running, and debugging AI agents or evaluation systems.
  • Ability to identify weaknesses in existing evaluation methods, develop new approaches, and rigorously test whether they work.
  • Experience designing rigorous experiments, analyzing model behavior, and investigating unexpected failures.
  • Familiarity with LLM/agent benchmarks, evaluation frameworks, or automated grading systems.
  • Experience independently driving research and engineering projects from problem identification through implementation and validation.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with adversarial testing, red teaming, reward hacking, or specification

In September 2026 we raised a $350 million Series E at a $3.5 billion valuation, and we are scaling our engineering and research teams to meet demand.

The role

Frontier AI data is expensive to make and hard to measure. Every task we deliver is tested against the strongest models, often through many long-running agent rollouts. Your job is to make that process faster, cheaper, and more rigorous with ML and AI

You will be one of the early members of ML & Research Engineering at Snorkel. You will study how frontier-grade data is generated and evaluated, form hypotheses, validate them against real production data, and ship the winners at scale. You will shape the discipline's direction, its standards, and the team that grows around it.

What you'll work on

  • Efficient agentic evals. Cut the cost of long-horizon agent evaluation with adaptive sampling, statistically grounded early stopping, model cascades, caching, and cheap-first gating.
  • AI model routing. Route every eval and judge call to the cheapest model that clears the quality bar, with fallback, monitoring, and cost attribution.
  • Fine-tuned small models. Fine-tune and serve open-weight models (LoRA and other parameter-efficient methods) where they match frontier quality, and know when they don't.
  • Predictive difficulty. Build models that estimate how hard a task is for frontier systems before running a single rollout.
  • Measurement for AI data. Build golden datasets, quantify the accuracy and calibration of LLM-as-judge systems, and make quality reproducible across projects.
  • Research to production. Turn research prototypes into reusable, configurable components that forward deployed engineers and researchers use on every project.

What you'll bring

  • 5+ years building production ML or software systems, with end-to-end ownership from prototype to production
  • Hands-on experience running LLM or ML workloads in production, and comfort reasoning about non-deterministic systems
  • Deep grounding in statistics and experimentation: experiment design, hypothesis testing, sampling, and confidence intervals
  • Strong Python and software engineering fundamentals, including testing, code review, and system design
  • Experience designing evaluations and interpreting results rigorously
  • A habit of finding high-impact problems before they are assigned, and clear communication with researchers, engineers, and business partners

Nice to have

  • Fine-tuning and serving open-weight models, and judging when a smaller model meets the quality bar
  • Building LLM evaluation or experimentation platforms, model gateways, or routing systems
  • Experience with agentic workloads, benchmarks, or RL environments
  • A record of taking research into production: publications, open-source work, or shipped research-driven features
  • MS or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, or a related field

Why join now

  • Frontier problems. Measure and shape the tasks designed to challenge the strongest models in the world.
  • All AI, no plumbing.

jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the SambaNova Summer 2027 Internship Program 

At SambaNova, our internship program is designed to give you hands-on experience tackling meaningful engineering challenges with real product impact. Because we are continuously evolving our program to provide the best possible experience, specific details and programming may vary by team and location, though you can generally expect the following: 

  • Program Structure & Duration: Our summer internships are structured as a 12-week experience, kicking off with onboarding and orientation, followed by mid-program check-ins, and wrapping up with final project presentations to your team and key stakeholders. 
  • Dedicated Mentorship: To support your growth, interns are typically paired with both a manager and a peer host/mentor who provide structured mentorship, technical guidance, and project alignment throughout the summer. 
  • Locations & Onsite Experience: Roles are based onsite at one of our global hubs— including San Jose (HQ), Austin, Bangalore, or Stockholm—to foster direct collaboration, community, and hands-on exposure to our teams and technology. (Note: Specific location availability varies by role.) 
  • Community & Engagement: Depending on your location and cohort schedule, programming may include leadership fireside chats, workshops, hackathons, lab tours, and social outings to help you connect with fellow interns and leaders across the company. 
  • Feedback & Future Opportunities: Throughout the program, you will receive structured feedback on your technical depth, ownership, collaboration, and project impact. High-performing interns may be considered for returning internships or full time opportunities upon graduation, subject to business needs and performance. 

About the Team 

The Runtime team owns the lowest level of the SambaNova software stack, the layer that talks directly to the hardware. We build the user libraries, drivers, networking, and system tools that run ML training and inference across SambaStack and SambaCloud. 

About the Role 

As a Runtime Engineer Intern, you'll write code in C/C++/Rust and Python on a scoped project across drivers, user space libraries, networking, or system tools. You'll get exposure to driver bring-up on next generation silicon, help test runtime features on large multi-node systems, and learn how to track down performance bottlenecks alongside the hardware and compiler teams. A dedicated mentor will guide you throughout the internship.

  • Contribute to kernel drivers for next generation SambaNova silicon 
  • Help build user space libraries that make efficient use of hardware resources Investigate networking bottlenecks within and across nodes 
  • Build or extend tools for profiling, debugging, and job and hardware management Help test runtime features on large multi-node systems

This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, SPACE - Sandbox Platform)
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

SPACE is Perplexity's sandbox platform. It's the isolated execution layer behind Perplexity Computer, the public Sandbox API, and a growing set of agent products. Every time an agent writes code, runs a tool, opens a browser, builds an app, or works on a user's files, it runs inside a SPACE sandbox.

We built our own sandbox platform that lets us build the exact platform our products need: real pause and resume, forking, rolling snapshots, credential isolation, fine-grained network policy, and enterprise-grade encryption. The work spans low-level virtualization and networking, distributed state machines, petabyte storage, and careful API design. Reliability, security, and cold-start latency are all things our customers feel directly.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design and build core sandbox infrastructure for running untrusted, agent-generated code safely, quickly, and at scale.

 - Own sandbox isolation and security end to end, working with Security Engineering on defense in depth for compute, networking, storage, and sensitive information.

 - Build stateful systems that manage long-lived execution environments and keep user data durable and correct through failures.

 - Drive performance and efficiency across the stack, from startup latency and resource density to cost.

 - Run sandbox infrastructure as an always-on production service, setting the bar for reliability, observability, capacity planning, and incident response.

 - Define clear platform interfaces and APIs so internal teams and external developers can build on sandboxes with confidence.

 - Provide technical leadership: mentor engineers, write clear design docs, and make long-term architectural decisions that keep the platform simple, secure, and able to evolve.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience designing and running production backend or infrastructure systems

 - Strong distributed systems experience: you've built and operated systems that coordinate state across many nodes, and you're fluent in consistency, consensus or leader election, idempotency, retries, and failure handling at scale.

 - Strong system design skills for stateful systems where correctness under failure matters.

 - Hands-on experience with Linux systems and modern infrastructure (for example AWS, Kubernetes, and container or VM runtimes).

 - Comfortable with security-sensitive systems and making pragmatic trade-offs between isolation, performance, and velocity.

 - Collaborative mindset and eagerness to work on hard problems with other experienced engineers.
   
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor, KVM, gVisor, Kata, or other virtualization and sandboxing technology.

 - Experience with snapshotting, copy-on-write filesystems, or block storage.

 - Experience with Linux networking (namespaces, eBPF, egress filtering) or secrets and key management.

 - Experience with custom scheduling, multi-cluster orchestration, or distributed state machines.

 - Experience building developer-facing APIs and SDKs, or code execution and agent infrastructure.

If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every qualification listed above.

jobs.description:
The Human Frontier Collective (HFC)’s mission is to bring the world's best minds to shape the future of AI – because the future of AI depends not only on powerful models, but on the people who teach them to think. We bring together researchers, academics, and domain leaders across 70+ fields – over 90% of members hold doctorates – to shape how frontier AI systems are built, evaluated, and governed. HFC members have since co-authored published work including SciPredict, PropensityBench, and Professional Reasoning Benchmark.

Why join the HFC

HFC centers on three core pillars: the network itself, participation in selected AI/ML projects, and opportunities to publish with our research team.

  • Join a unique and exclusive expert network: You’ll become a part of an interdisciplinary community, consisting of over 90% doctorates and field leaders representing 70+ fields from the leading institutions. We’re a collective of top innovators and thought leaders committed to advancing frontier AI to power the world’s most important decisions.
  • Participate in AI/ML projects: Beyond the collective network, you’ll be regularly invited to work on high-impact projects with Scale AI and its affiliated lab and platform: building AI safety and policy guardrails, helping models understand real-world deep learning workflows by designing, reviewing, and optimizing PyTorch models, evaluating complex ML code and AI-generated implementations for efficiency and correctness, and more.
  • Co-author selected research publications: Collaborate with Scale’s research team to co-author technical reports and research papers—boosting your academic visibility and professional recognition.

Who should apply

  • Background: PhD, or postdoctoral research experience, in Machine Learning, Computer Science, or a related field; or senior industry experience in Machine Learning or a related field.
  • Skills: Strong proficiency in Python and modern ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow). Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS) and MLOps tools (Docker) and LLM frameworks (LangChain) is a plus.
  • Professional Mindset: Detail-oriented, innovative thinker with a passion for applied AI research and a commitment to collaboration.

How it works

  • Duration: This is a fully remote opportunity with no fixed end date; engagements continue as long as there's mutual interest. This is a 1099 independent contractor engagement. 
  • Work authorization: We do not sponsor visas for Fellows. To participate in the HFC Fellows program, you need to have or independently obtain full-time work authorization in the country you reside in. 
  • Community Network: Once you’ve received an invitation to join the HFC, you’ll also gain access to our newsletters, discussion channels, virtual sessions, IRL events, and much more.
  • Projects Logistics: 
    • Project selection: You’ll regularly get matched to carefully selected projects from our partners. Depending on the partner, projects range from evaluating AI models to designing experiments, building RL environments, co-authoring research papers, and more. 
    • Flexible schedule: There's no minimum commitment – you decide whether to take on a project. Most fellows spend 10–25 hours per week, on a schedule they set themselves.
    • Competitive pay: Project pay rates vary across platforms and depend on a number of factors, including but not limited to: projects

AI is no different, except it touches everything instead of one slice, and the window to build the layer underneath it is open right now.

jobs.title: Quality Engineering Technician
jobs.description:
Figure is an AI robotics company developing autonomous general-purpose humanoid robots. The goal of the company is to ship humanoid robots with human level intelligence. Its robots are engineered to perform a variety of tasks in the home and commercial markets. Figure is headquartered in San Jose, CA.

The Production Quality Technician will actively work on the manufacturing line and ensure the manufacturing processes are meeting design and manufacturing specifications.   • Take the lead on initiating containment activities for production quality issues.

  • Study the manufacturing processes and identify potential quality risks.

  • Participate in Material Review Board activities.

  • Experience with root cause analysis and CAPA methodologies (8D, 5-Why, fishbone/Ishikawa).

Bedrock Robotics, Inc. seeks a Hardware Engineer in San Francisco, CA responsible for designing, manufacturing, and testing its autonomous hardware systems, including high performance computer systems, sensors, controllers, interfaces to machines, and testing equipment.

This position will work with autonomous hardware systems installed on standard heavy construction machinery—excavators, bulldozers, and wheel loaders—to allow that equipment to perform earthmoving work on construction sites autonomously. In this context, “autonomous hardware systems” are the physical electronic components installed on a construction machine that allow it to operate without a human operator in the cab. They consist of: high-performance computer systems (ruggedized onboard computers mounted on the machine that perform the calculations required for autonomous operation); sensors (devices that allow the machine to perceive its surroundings, including cameras, radar, lidar, and GNSS); controllers and interfaces (electronic units that translate the computer's decisions into electrical signals that operate the machine's existing hydraulic, steering, and engine controls); and testing equipment (benches, fixtures, and instrumentation used to verify each of the above components before and after installation on a machine). Working together, these systems continuously collect sensor data, determine the machine's position and what is around it, calculate the path the machine should follow and the movements it should make, and then command the machine's controls to carry out those movements, performing the tasks a human operator would otherwise perform manually.

Specific duties include: (i) defining and designing hardware systems, including component-level architecture for autonomous machines and camera/optics design and performance; (ii) establishing and leading relationships and programs with external vendors to facilitate hardware manufacturing and delivery; (iii) supporting hardware system verification and validation, including working with safety teams to establish/tune requirements and performance metrics for components and systems; (iv) using industry standard tools and knowledge to test standards of hardware systems; and (v) writing reusable, high quality sensor data analysis and testing automation software.

This is a hybrid office-based/work-from-home position within the United States. The employee can work remotely from within the United States but must be able to work in the San Francisco office at least three (3) days per week.

Must have a bachelor’s degree (or foreign equivalent) in Electrical Engineering, Robotics Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a directly related field plus five (5) years of progressively responsible, post-baccalaureate experience in designing, integrating, and validating electrical hardware systems.

Must have any experience with: (i) high performance computer systems, including x86 or ARM; (ii) robotics sensors stacks, including lidar, radar, camera, or GNSS; (iii) communication protocols and technologies, including CAN, LIN, J1939, FlexRay, or Ethernet; (iv) python or C++/C/Rust; and (v) standardization tools and organizations, including ISO, SAE, and ANSI.

Must be willing and able to travel regionally/nationally up to 15%, to visit hardware testing sites.

Experience can be concurrent.

This position is expected to pay an annual salary of $236,000.

Apply online at bedrockrobotics.com/careers http://bedrockrobotics.com/careers.

jobs.title: Principal Place and Route (PnR) Engineer
jobs.location: Austin, Texas, United States; San Jose, California, United States
jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the team

The Place and Route team writes the software that maps dataflow graphs onto SambaNova’s Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit (RDU). Our tools partition each graph, place the pieces on the chip’s compute and memory units, and route the communication between them. The quality of that mapping sets the throughput of the compiled program, including large language model inference and training. We are looking to grow our team with highly motivated engineers who want to utilize advanced algorithms to solve challenging problems. 

About the Role

You will develop and tune the partitioning, placement, and routing algorithms that map customer workloads onto the RDU. You will work with the compiler team, hardware architects, and performance engineers to model new hardware constraints and trace throughput gaps back to mapping decisions. Your changes will ship in production releases and show up in measured performance.

Responsibilities

  • Develop partitioning, placement, and routing algorithms that meet hardware resource constraints and keep compile times practical
  • Tune PnR results for target workloads, including LLM inference at different batch sizes and concurrency levels
  • Model new hardware constraints and architecture features in our solvers and heuristics as the chip evolves
  • Analyze compiled output with performance engineers and trace throughput gaps back to mapping decisions
  • Build the infrastructure for prototyping, regression testing, and deployment of PnR changes
  • Work with the compiler and hardware teams to define interfaces and resource models

Required Qualifications

  • M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related field
  • 3+ years of experience developing optimization or graph algorithms in industry or research
  • Expert knowledge of graph algorithms, partitioning algorithms, combinatorial optimization, or MILP solvers
  • Strong proficiency in C/C++
  • Familiarity with Python
  • Experience designing large, highly parallel, performance-sensitive systems
  • Ability to learn hardware architecture and apply it to improve performance
  • Experience solving NP-hard problems in practice with heuristics, approximation, or pruned exact methods

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with place and route for FPGAs, CGRAs, or other spatial architectures
  • Experience with ML compilers such as MLIR, LLVM, TVM, or XLA
  • Experience with simulated annealing, constraint programming, or SAT/SMT solvers
  • Familiarity with LLM inference stacks such as vLLM and PyTorch
  • Publications at venues such as FPGA, DAC, ICCAD, or MLSys

jobs.description:
Technical Customer Support Specialist (Contract, Remote)

Who we are A global team united by curiosity and a shared mission: to be the first choice for AI audio. We're building a new category of technology from the ground up — moving fast, holding ourselves to a high bar, and giving everyone the autonomy to do their best work. The best idea wins, regardless of where it comes from.

About the role As a Technical Customer Support Specialist, you'll be on the front lines with our enterprise and B2B customers — helping them get the most out of ElevenLabs, including our API and the ElevenAgents platform, which orchestrates LLMs, telephony, and other AI integrations.  - Solid understanding of APIs and how developers integrate them; comfortable reading and troubleshooting code, especially Python or JavaScript

 - A genuine interest in implementing and experimenting with AI solutions — not just supporting them from the outside

 - Experience working autonomously in a fast-moving, international, remote team

 - Passionate about AI and the problems it can solve — you follow the space closely and have opinions about it

 - Analytically sharp with a first-principles approach to debugging and problem-solving

The DevOps Engineer is responsible for supporting and improving cloud and ML/AI infrastructure, automating deployments, and maintaining CI/CD pipelines to ensure efficient, secure, and scalable development workflows. This role plays a crucial part in infrastructure automation, monitoring, and cloud security while collaborating with Software and ML Engineers, Product support, QA, and Security teams.

As a key member of the DevOps team, the DevOps Engineer helps manage cloud environments, CI/CD pipelines, and Infrastructure as Code (IaC), ensuring high availability and compliance with security best practices.

In this role, you’ll get to:

Cloud Infrastructure, Security & Reliability

• Support and maintain scalable, highly available, and secure cloud infrastructure in accordance with company policies and standards.
• Provision and manage cloud resources using Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Terragrunt, CloudFormation).
• Implement cloud security best practices, including IAM/role-based access controls, encryption, vulnerability management, and secure infrastructure configurations.
• Support containerized environments and orchestration platforms.
• Apply DevSecOps principles across infrastructure and deployment workflows.
• Participate in disaster recovery planning, testing, and recovery activities.

CI/CD, Automation & Deployment

• Maintain and optimize CI/CD pipelines using tools such as GitLab CI/CD and Jenkins, supporting application and ML model deployments.
• Improve deployment reliability and support zero-downtime deployment strategies.
• Automate configuration management, infrastructure provisioning, and routine operational processes.
• Troubleshoot deployment and pipeline issues and implement improvements to prevent recurrence.
• Develop scripts and automation to reduce manual work and improve engineering efficiency.

AI & Agentic Infrastructure

• Help design, deploy, operate, and secure infrastructure supporting AI and agentic products, including MCP, agents, integrations, internal tooling, and customer-facing use cases.
• Use AI-assisted engineering tools, coding copilots, and AI-driven troubleshooting to improve DevOps productivity and reduce repetitive operational work.
• Evaluate and adopt practical AI-enabled workflows that improve infrastructure management, troubleshooting, and operational efficiency.

MLOps & ML Platform Infrastructure

• Operate and scale ML platform infrastructure, including Databricks and Sagemaker clusters, jobs compute, ML pipelines, and Model Serving endpoints.
• Manage production model-serving infrastructure, including compute capacity, provisioned throughput, and autoscaling for high-throughput inference workloads.
• Maintain infrastructure-level monitoring for model drift, data quality, inference performance, and serving health, while partnering with ML Engineering on model evaluation, quality thresholds, and model correctness.
• Partner with ML Engineering to support reliable CI/CD and production deployment of ML models.

Observability, Incident Response & Engineering Collaboration

• Maintain monitoring, logging, metrics, and alerting solutions using tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, Coralogix, and CloudWatch.
• Support incident response and perform Root Cause Analysis (RCA) for infrastructure and deployment-related issues.
• Improve system observability through effective log aggregation, metrics collection, monitoring, and alerting.
• Partner with Software Engineers, ML Engineers, QA, and Software Engineers in Test to improve deployment workflows and integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines.
• Collaborate with IT Security to maintain secure cloud operations and infrastructure policies.
• Respond to engineering and Product Support requests in a timely manner and provide technical infrastructure support when needed.
• Maintain accurate internal technical and operational documentation.
• Collaborate effectively with international teams across multiple time zones

jobs.title: Senior Staff Software Engineer, Backend - AI Native (Evergreen)
jobs.description:
Innovate with purpose

At BILL, we believe in empowering the businesses that drive our economy. By replacing outdated financial processes with innovative tools, we help businesses—from startups to established brands—make smarter decisions and gain control of their operations. And we don’t stop there: we’re creating the future of financial automation so businesses can spend more time on what matters.

Working here means you become part of a vision-driven team that’s ready to tackle challenges and build cutting-edge solutions. We value purpose, drive, and curiosity—and we thrive in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment. We're remote-first, with office spaces in San Jose, CA and Draper, UT — and opportunities to connect in person when it counts. BILLders collaborate to deliver real impact for businesses that need more time in their busy weeks.

BILL builds high performing teams and we seek to hire the best talent for every role. We're committed to building a workplace that fosters inclusion and diverse perspectives, valuing each person’s unique skills and experiences. We’d love to hear from you—you might be just what we’re looking for, whether in this role or another.

✨ Let’s give businesses more time for what matters.

Make your impact at a leading Fintech Company

BILL's accounts payable, accounts receivable and accountant products move money for hundreds of thousands of small and midsize businesses. We are rebuilding the backend behind these products so that every capability is built once, in a clean API, and is available to web, mobile, developer APIs and AI agents on the same day.

As a Senior Staff Backend Engineer, you will rebuild core AP and AR services. You will design the domain models and API contracts, migrate behavior out of legacy code, and use AI coding agents as a core part of how you work. This is a hands-on product engineering role in a domain where correctness matters: the code you ship decides whether a payment is approved, scheduled and sent.

In this role you will:
• Rebuild core AP and AR backend capabilities (bills, invoices, payments, approvals, vendors and customers) as well-bounded services with consistent, well-documented APIs.
• Build each capability once, headless. Move business rules out of the UI and legacy code paths into the service layer, and expose it through our federated GraphQL API for web, mobile and AI agents, and through REST for developers and partners. A capability is done when it is ready for all of them, not when it works in the web UI.
• Apply and help shape BILL's API standards: common types defined once across REST, GraphQL and events, consistent list APIs, business operations as explicit actions with server-owned status, idempotent writes for anything that moves money, and errors a developer or an AI agent can act on. Enforce them in code, not in review, with contract tests, schema checks and linters in CI.
• Work AI-first across the whole software lifecycle, from design through production, as described in the next section.
• Migrate live, high-volume financial workflows and their APIs without breaking customers or consumers: parity tests, staged rollouts, dual writes, backfills, reconciliation and rollback paths for data; additive changes, expand-and-contract and deprecation windows for contracts.
• Make APIs usable by AI agents as well as people: self-describing schemas with documentation an LLM can read, responses that return related data in one call instead of many, and AI tools that are a thin layer over the same queries and mutations that web, mobile and internal clients use.
• Own reliability for what you build: observability, on-call readiness, performance and data integrity.
• Raise the bar for the engineers around you through design reviews, code reviews and mentoring.

How you will work: AI-first across the lifecycle

AI-first here means rethinking how the work gets done across the whole software lifecycle, from design through production, not running the old process

jobs.title: AI Systems Engineer - Data & State Management - Senior
jobs.description:
Location: Anywhere in Country

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity

We are seeking an AI Systems Engineer to own the stateful backbone of EY’s AI-native platform, including the data stores, memory tiers, and event streaming systems that hold and move every piece of state in EY’s Hybrid AI Multi-Environment Runtime (HAI). This role ensures that agentic AI workloads have durable, performant, and consistent access to data across cloud, on-prem, edge, client-managed, and air-gapped environments.

Within HAI, this is a distinct discipline from platform operations and model serving. This role owns everything that must remember, persist, or flow: relational and key-value state, vector and graph stores, object storage, durable workflows, and the streaming and change-data-capture pipelines that connect them. It is the layer that makes the platform stateful, reliable, and event-driven.

It is ideal for a data-infrastructure engineer who is equally comfortable operating production databases and high-throughput streaming systems, who treats data durability, consistency, and recoverability as non-negotiable in regulated client contexts, and who understands that state is the hardest part of any distributed platform to get right.

Your Key Responsibilities

• Own the memory and data stores: relational and durable state (PostgreSQL, DBOS durable workflows), caching (Redis/Valkey), vector stores (Qdrant/Milvus/PGVector), knowledge graphs (Neo4j), and object/block storage (MinIO, OpenEBS Mayastor), across every environment and tenant.
• Own event streaming and async messaging: Apache Kafka (Strimzi), NATS JetStream (agent-to-agent), Debezium (change data capture), Apache Flink (stream processing), and Apicurio/CloudEvents (schema and event contracts).
• Own data durability, consistency, and recoverability: replication, backup/restore, point-in-time recovery, and cross-environment data movement, tiered by RPO/RTO.
• Build and operate streaming and CDC pipelines that move data reliably between stores and services, with schema governance and evolution that prevents breaking changes across producers and consumers.
• Make state multi-tenant and portable, ensuring isolation, performance, and consistent semantics whether running on managed cloud services or self-hosted OSS in an air-gapped environment.
• Provide the data and lineage substrate that downstream governance, observability, and AI knowledge capabilities depend on, as well as integrating with lineage tooling.

Skills And Attributes For Success

• Deep expertise operating production databases and data stores at scale, including relational, key-value, vector, graph, and object storage.
• Strong command of streaming and event-driven architectures (Kafka, NATS, CDC, stream processing) and the consistency tradeoffs they involve.
• A durability-first mindset: thinking in terms of consistency, recoverability, blast radius, and data correctness under failure.
• Ability to operate stateful systems consistently across managed cloud and self-hosted OSS in cloud, on-prem, edge, and air-gapped environments.
• Strong grasp of schema governance and evolution, preventing breaking changes across producers and consumers.
• Strong communicator able to guide consuming teams toward the right storage and streaming patterns.
• Orientation toward reliability and toil reduction through automation and infrastructure-as-code for data systems.

To qualify you must have

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or related technical field.
• 8+ years operating production data infrastructure, streaming systems, or database platforms at scale.
• Hands-on expertise with relational databases (PostgreSQL) and caching (Redis/Valkey), including HA, replication, and backup/recovery.
• Exposure to AI/ML data

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Enterprise Brain
jobs.description:
About Glean:
 
Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles.
 
At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level.
 
Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality.
 
If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company.

About the Role:

Glean’s Enterprise Brain team builds applied ML systems that help Glean understand a user’s work and anticipate useful next steps, including task prediction and proactive assistance. The work combines LLMs and traditional ML with signals from the Enterprise Graph, ranking and retrieval, and orchestration. You’ll own production ML problems from problem definition and evaluation through launch and monitoring, with a focus on measurable improvements to product quality.

You will:

  • Define and solve applied ML problems involving user-work understanding, task prediction, and proactive assistance.
  • Combine LLMs and traditional ML with Enterprise Graph signals, ranking/retrieval, and orchestration to improve product quality.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer: Computer Vision for People Understanding
jobs.description:
At Apple, individual creativity converges around shared values that drive innovation. Our CV/ML team works where perception, intelligence, and real-time processing meet. We have shipped Optic ID, Apple Vision Pro's biometric authentication, along with Eye Tracking and other computer vision features. We are looking for an experienced CV/ML engineer who runs rigorous experiments, shapes the data behind them, and brings modern deep learning architectures to products used by millions of people.

Ready to make an impact?

Description

You will take on complex problems in understanding people from camera and sensor data, and you will own these problems from hypothesis to shipped model. You will shape experiments and what success looks like, and you will bring new methods where the established ones fall short. You know that model quality starts with the data: you find gaps and imbalances in it and work with partner teams to get the data that's missing. You will represent your area to hardware, software, and UX teams and adapt recent architectures for efficient on-device use.

Minimum Qualifications

B.S. and minimum 10 years of industry experience in Machine Learning, Computer Vision or related field.
Hands-on experience training and evaluating deep learning models for vision.
Proficiency in Python and PyTorch.
Track record of designing experiments and drawing sound conclusions.

Preferred Qualifications

M.S. or Ph.D. in Machine Learning, Computer Vision or related field.
Experience in face or eye analysis or biometrics: detection, landmarks, tracking, gaze estimation, or recognition.
Experience curating large datasets and specifying data collection, including synthetic data.
Strong foundations in linear algebra, probability, and optimization.
Familiarity with optimizing models for deployment.
Experience shipping ML in consumer products, publishing at top-tier CV/ML conferences, or holding patents.
Expertise across multiple technical areas, solving cross-disciplinary challenges, and explaining the end-to-end system.
Track record of independently driving significant, ambiguous problems to resolution, with cross-functional impact, and setting technical direction with management and beyond.
Experience mentoring beyond your own team and communicating with senior leadership.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills, and a curiosity for hard problems.

Job Title: AI/ML Data Platform Engineer (Senior) (Onsite)

Location: Linthicum, MD, 21090

Duration: Upto 7 Years

Position Description: The Senior AI/ML Data Platform Engineer will be expected to design, build, and operationalize machine learning infrastructure and AI-driven data solutions on AWS. The successful candidate will bridge data engineering and MLOps, ensuring scalable, secure, and compliant AI/ML pipelines that support advanced analytics and decision-making across programs.

The AI/ML Data Platform Engineer creates and/or maintains operating systems, communications software, database packages, compilers, repositories, and utility and assembler programs. This position is responsible for modifying existing software and developing special-purpose software to ensure efficiency and integrity between systems and applications.

Key Responsibilities
• Design and implement end-to-end ML pipelines including data ingestion, feature engineering, model training, validation, and deployment on AWS (SageMaker, Glue, Lambda, Step Functions).
• Build and maintain MLOps infrastructure: model registries, CI/CD for ML models, experiment tracking (MLflow or SageMaker Experiments), and automated retraining pipelines.
• Develop scalable feature stores and data preprocessing pipelines using AWS Glue, EMR, or Spark on Databricks.
• Partner with data scientists and analysts to productionize models and translate research prototypes into robust, maintainable systems.
• Ensure ML systems meet government data security, privacy (PII/PHI handling), and compliance requirements (FISMA, NIST).
• Implement data versioning, lineage tracking, and model explainability/audit capabilities.
• Monitor deployed models for drift, performance degradation, and data quality issues; implement alerting and automated remediation.
• Contribute to data platform architecture decisions, including lakehouse design, data cataloging (AWS Glue Data Catalog / Apache Atlas), and access controls.
• Document architectures, pipeline designs, and operational runbooks to government documentation standards.

Education: This position requires a Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with a major in computer science, information systems, engineering, business, or other related scientific or technical discipline. Three (3) years of equivalent experience in a related field may be substituted for the Bachelor’s degree. (Note: A Master’s degree is preferred.)

General Experience: The proposed candidate must have twelve (12) years of computer experience in information systems design. Other experience required:
• 6+ years of data engineering or software engineering experience, with 2+ years focused on ML platform or MLOps engineering.
• Deep expertise with AWS ML/AI services: SageMaker, Glue, EMR, Lambda, Step Functions, Kinesis, S3.
• Strong Python skills; experience with ML frameworks (scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, XGBoost).
• Experience building and maintaining MLOps pipelines and CI/CD for ML workflows.
• Solid understanding of distributed computing (Spark/EMR) and large-scale data processing.
• Familiarity with government data security requirements and experience operating in FedRAMP-authorized AWS environments.
• Experience with infrastructure-as-code tools (Terraform, AWS CDK, CloudFormation).

Specialized Experience: The proposed candidate must have at least ten (10) years of experience in IT systems analysis and programming including the following:
• Experience with generative AI / LLM integration (AWS Bedrock, LangChain) in enterprise or government contexts.
• Knowledge of responsible AI, model governance, and bias detection frameworks.
• Experience with real-time/streaming ML pipelines using Kinesis or Kafka.
• Familiarity with data mesh or federated data architectures.
• Background in healthcare, public health, or social services data (HIPAA/42 CFR Part 2 awareness).

Preferred Certifications
• AWS Certified Machine Learning — Specialty
• AWS Certified

jobs.title: Manager, Delivery Solutions Architects - Financial Services

jobs.description:
CSQ427R268

You will build and lead a team of Delivery Solution Architects (DSAs) responsible for the post-sales success of Databricks' largest Financial Services customers. This is one of the most consequential delivery leadership roles in the company. The customers in your portfolio anchor a strategic vertical for Databricks, and your team's work directly determines how quickly Data and AI transforms how they do business.

As a DSA Manager you set the technical strategy across your portfolio, decide where to invest your team's capacity, and partner with Sales, Pre-Sales, Professional Services, and our Systems Integrator ecosystem to move use cases from kickoff to production. You are a hands-on technical sponsor and trusted advisor to a select group of customers, including their C-suite. You build the systems, operating cadences, and playbooks that make your team and the broader DSA practice sharper over time.

The DSAs you lead are senior technical talent, drawn from principal-level solution architecture, top-tier consulting, or senior engineering backgrounds. Hiring, coaching, and growing this team is the heart of the job.

The impact you will have:

  • Hire, coach, and develop a high-performing DSA team. Own career growth, calibrated performance management, and individual development plans.
  • Own capacity planning and investment forecasting across the FINS portfolio. Defend investment decisions with data, alongside sales and field leadership.
  • Partner with Sales, Pre-Sales, Professional Services, and Systems Integrator partners to accelerate use case delivery and reduce customer risk.
  • Drive measurable customer outcomes: use-case throughput, time-to-production, consumption growth, and renewal rates. Forecast each across your portfolio.

CIVIL ENGINEER

SpaceXSI is seeking an exceptional Civil Engineer to lead the civil and site development design and delivery of our next-generation mission-critical data center campuses and co-located power generation facilities. You will architect resilient, high-performance civil infrastructure systems capable of supporting massive AI compute loads, ultra-dense power infrastructure, and rapid deployment timelines that set new industry benchmarks.

This is a high-impact, high-ownership role for an exceptional engineer who excels in fast-paced, technically demanding environments. You will combine deep expertise in land development, hydrology & hydraulics, and environmental systems with exceptional speed of execution, while seamlessly collaborating across structural, MEP, geotechnical, and construction teams to deliver facilities that power the future of AI.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own end-to-end civil and land development engineering for hyperscale data center campuses, power generation sites, turbine support areas, transformer yards, and industrial infrastructure — delivering complete site grading, stormwater management, underground utilities, and environmental compliance solutions on aggressive schedules
  • Lead detailed hydrology and hydraulics (H&H) analysis, floodplain modeling & analysis, stormwater design, retention/detention systems, and flood mitigation strategies for large-scale industrial sites
  • Design and optimize land development plans, including earthwork calculations, site grading, erosion/sediment control, cut/fill balancing, and foundation preparation for heavy industrial loads in data centers, power plants, and related environments
  • Perform advanced floodplain modeling, environmental assessments, regulatory permitting, and sustainability evaluations to ensure resilient and compliant site infrastructure
  • Drive cross-functional multidisciplinary coordination with structural, mechanical, electrical, geotechnical, and construction teams to integrate civil systems with foundations, power distribution, turbine infrastructure, underground utilities, and overall campus layouts
  • Provide expert civil input during site selection, geotechnical investigations, feasibility studies, and due diligence for data center and power generation projects, with particular focus on environmental constraints, floodplain risks, underground utilities, and industrial site challenges
  • Deliver rapid, high-quality responses to RFIs, submittals, and field inquiries while maintaining rigorous documentation and design intent
  • Conduct site visits and construction observations to verify earthwork, grading, drainage installation, underground utility placement, erosion control measures, and overall quality
  • Identify and implement innovative solutions in sustainable land development, low-impact development, advanced H&H modeling, floodplain resilience, and efficient underground utility networks to support SpaceXSI's aggressive growth trajectory

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist, Research & Applied Science
jobs.description:
Senior Data Scientist, Research & Applied Science

Location: Hoboken, NJ (on site)

About Faropoint

Faropoint owns and operates last-mile, Class B, small-bay industrial properties across 20+ U.S. markets. Our in-house technology team builds proprietary software and predictive models that shape what we buy, how we price leases, and which tenants we underwrite. It's a senior group that works side by side with the investors and asset managers who use its tools every day.

The Role

Our models estimate market rent, forecast lease renewals, price property sales, and score tenant credit risk. Their outputs feed multimillion-dollar decisions. Small-bay industrial is fragmented, comps are thin, and no two assets are alike. This is a judgment problem, not a big-data problem.

You'll be our senior data scientist: the person who can authoritatively explain how our models work, including to an investor's own data scientists, and who decides whether they're right and proves it. You'll set our standards for validation and experimentation, work with the Director of Research on what to test next, and mentor junior data scientists who help maintain the models. No real estate background is required.

What You'll Do

Own the core prediction models

• Retrain, improve, and extend our rent, lease renewal, sale pricing, and tenant credit models, plus entity de-duplication.

• Pick up the record of hundreds of past experiments, including the ones that failed, and turn it into a research baseline so we don't repeat them.

• Benchmark new approaches, including tabular foundation models, AutoML, and agent-driven automated research, against well-tuned gradient-boosted baselines. Adopt them only when they win on held-out, real-world outcomes.

• Test candidate data sources and features (drive time, location quality, zoning, site characteristics, our spatial layers) against actual leasing and sales outcomes, and decide what earns a place in the models.

Make the outputs trustworthy

• Build backtesting, error analysis, and monitoring so model outputs are verified before they reach decision-makers.

• Design experiments that stay honest at scale. Sealed holdouts, time- and location-aware splits, and multiple-comparison controls mean hundreds of automated experiments still produce conclusions you'd defend.

• Keep research reproducible: versioned training data, documented features, repeatable experiments. Document the models as they stand today, since the existing documentation is out of date.

Run models in production

• Own serving endpoints, drift monitoring, and a model registry with clear lineage. Make inference reliable and fast (batch prediction runs and SageMaker endpoints that don't fail under load) and keep serving costs in line with actual usage. You'll work on the AWS platform and deployment pipelines the platform engineer provides.

Evaluate our LLM pipelines

• Own the methodology for measuring how accurately LLMs extract data from leases and market reports: labeled datasets, calibrated automated graders, and a clear definition of what counts as a regression.

Partner with the business

• Turn questions from investment, research, and asset-management colleagues into analyses, and explain uncertainty in plain language.

• Represent our models externally when an investor or partner wants to understand them.

• Track developments in ML and AI, and bring back what proves useful on our problems.

What You'll Bring

Must-haves

• 6+ years of applied statistics or machine learning, including production models you kept owning after launch.

• Strong Python and SQL, and deep experience building predictive models on tabular data.

• Rigor in validation and experimentation: you know how a model can look better than it is, and you can explain error and uncertainty to a non-technical audience.

• Experience deploying and monitoring models in production on a cloud platform (AWS SageMaker or equivalent).

• Daily use of AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cu

Designs, builds and improves what the GTM Agent does to create pipeline, from the first signal about a prospect to a booked meeting. Owns the software and agents behind outbound on every channel: inbound lead follow-up, prospecting, multi-channel sequences, email deliverability, calling and the quality of every message the agent writes, with people deciding what goes out. Serves Sales Development Representatives (SDRs), Account Executives (AEs), their managers and Marketing.

The goal of the role is business impact for those teams: more positive replies, more meetings booked and more qualified pipeline for every dollar spent. Additionally, this role has a communication and evangelizing component: showing the teams it serves what works, and sharing content and open source projects with our developer community.

This role suits an engineer who has already built agents or software for outbound and prospecting, such as sequencing, email deliverability, dialing or AI-written outreach.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Spends time with SDRs, AEs and their managers to find the prospecting work they repeat that the agent can take over.

 - Designs, builds and improves the agent's outbound workflows: what starts each run, what the agent reads and decides, what it drafts, and what waits for a rep's approval.

 - Builds the agentic system that follows up every inbound lead within minutes: it qualifies the lead, researches the person and the account, and drafts a first touch for the owner the routing rules assign.

 - Builds and improves the system that runs Marketing's outbound plays and campaigns for every rep, from the target list to the first touch.

 - Builds the software and agentic system behind multi-channel sequences, which combine email, LinkedIn and calls, choose each next touch from what the prospect did, and stop when the prospect replies on any channel.

 - Builds the email sending and deliverability system: sending domains and mailboxes, warm-up, daily limits, address checks, bounces, opt-outs and inbox placement across mail providers.

 - Builds the calling software reps use: call lists, dialing and the research a rep reads before each call.

 - Owns the quality of what the agent writes, so every message fits the prospect's signal, their history with us and the right product, and uses how much reps edit each message and the replies it gets to find what to fix.

 - Builds the safeguards that keep prospects from getting duplicate or overlapping outreach, and the sync that logs every email, LinkedIn action and call in Salesforce.

 - Builds experiments that test messages, channels, timing and sequences against held-out groups, measures which ones book meetings, and fixes or removes what doesn't.

 - Writes evals for every feature shipped, and ships each feature with its scorecard row.

 - Shows reps and their managers what works, and shares it through blog posts, webinars and open source.

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Integrity
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Integrity team protects people and businesses using ChatGPT, Codex, and the API from fraud, abuse, and harmful misuse. Our work spans payment and promotional abuse, compromised accounts and API credentials, business and advertiser integrity, and emerging misuse of frontier AI capabilities. We also help product teams measure authentic usage so that abuse doesn’t distort decisions about how our products are growing.

Integrity Data Science helps teams decide where to intervene and whether those interventions work. A payment control can prevent fraud while blocking legitimate purchases. A product launch can make it easier for customers to get started while creating new opportunities for abuse. We measure both sides of those decisions.



ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Data Scientist on Integrity, you’ll find emerging abuse patterns, size their impact, and lead the analytical work behind decisions about detection, enforcement, and product launches. You’ll work with Product, Engineering, Research, Policy, and Operations to turn findings into improvements and measure what happens after they ship.

 - Investigate anomalous activity across products. Estimate how common a problem is, who is affected, and what it costs users or the business. Use that evidence to recommend where to focus.

 - Define outcome metrics and guardrails, establish baselines, and build monitoring that surfaces changes in abuse, customer friction, and operational performance.

 - Help build and evaluate detection rules, classifiers, and human review workflows. Use labeled samples and review outcomes to understand what the systems miss, where they flag legitimate activity, and how those errors vary across users and products.

 - Design randomized holdouts and use quasi-experimental or observational methods when randomization is impractical. Estimate harm or fraud losses prevented alongside effects on legitimate users, revenue, compute costs, and review workload. Recommend whether to launch, expand, adjust, or retire a control.

 - Trace where signals, review decisions, or enforcement actions break down. Work with partners to close gaps and build reusable datasets, analyses, and investigation tools.



IDEAL CANDIDATE

 - You use AI tools to investigate large, messy datasets, test hypotheses quickly, and automate recurring analyses. You’re fluent in SQL and Python and can verify AI-generated queries, code, and conclusions against the underlying data.

 - You have strong statistical judgment and experience with experimentation, causal inference, or observational analysis. You can reason from incomplete or biased labels and explain how uncertainty affects a decision.

 - You take ownership of open-ended problems, from deciding what to measure through recommending an action and checking whether it worked.

 - You communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical partners and can explain the tradeoffs behind a recommendation.

 - Experience in integrity, trust and safety, fraud or risk analytics, security analytics, or applied ML evaluation is helpful. Experience evaluating detection systems, human review, or LLM-based classifiers is a plus.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

jobs.title: Japan Chief Architect
jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

We are building a next-generation AI inference accelerator and the rack-scale system around it, in Japan, on a leading-edge domestic 2nm process. The work is funded through a multi-year national programme to establish sovereign AI infrastructure, and runs from architecture definition through test silicon, full chip tape-out, and deployment of production racks.

We are looking for the architect who will define the chip and technically lead the team that builds it, working with the US HQ engineering team. You will decide how compute, memory and interconnect are balanced for large language model inference, and what the hardware exposes to the compiler and runtime. You understand the software stack as well as the silicon, and you stay with the architecture through RTL, verification and physical implementation until it works in silicon.

What you will own

  • The chip architecture and microarchitecture specification for a reconfigurable dataflow accelerator: tile architecture, on-chip network, memory hierarchy, and the execution model that maps AI workloads onto them.
  • The hardware and software interface: the programming model, control interfaces, and the assumptions the compiler and runtime are allowed to make about the hardware.
  • Technical leadership of the implementation, from architecture through RTL, verification and physical design, to tape-out and silicon correlation.

Responsibilities

Architecture definition

  • Define the chip and system architecture against inference performance requirements: tokens per second per user, aggregate throughput, and tokens per second per watt.
  • Use performance models and architectural simulations to decide trade-offs, and keep them calibrated against measured silicon as it becomes available.
  • Make the balance calls across compute capability, memory bandwidth and interconnect bandwidth, and defend each one with data.

Hardware and software co-design

  • Work directly with compiler, runtime and model optimization engineers so that the architecture is one the software stack can actually exploit.
  • Own the interfaces that software depends on: mapping, scheduling, memory allocation, synchronization, power, and scale-up and scale-out networks.
  • Analyse real LLM workloads (attention, KV cache, quantized and low-precision arithmetic, batching) on the architecture, and feed the results back into both the hardware and the software.

Technical leadership of implementation

  • Lead the team technically from specification to tape-out: microarchitecture specs, RTL design reviews, block interfaces, clocking, reset and power domains.
  • Set verification goals with the verification lead, and ensure performance correlation between the architectural model and the RTL.
  • Assess physical feasibility early and keep the design within it: area and timing budgets, floorplan partitioning, power, thermal limits, and die and package size.
  • Lead technical design reviews at each integration milestone, and give the technical sign-off for tape-out.

jobs.title: FinOps Specialist, Production Engineering
jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.



Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

 - One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

 - If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

 - We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

 - We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

 - We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.




OUR TEAMS

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across five areas:

 - Compute — the foundation for running Ramp’s services and financial workflows: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and asynchronous execution and messaging systems, including Temporal. The team owns production runtime reliability, scaling, isolation, and safe rollouts.

 - Storage — the production data foundations that underpin Ramp: databases, caching, and object storage, with ownership of reliability, performance, capacity, recovery, and safe data movement.

 - Developer Infrastructure — the shared infrastructure that helps engineers ship and understand production: CI/CD systems, observability foundations for logs, metrics, and traces, and visibility into infrastructure usage and cost.

 - Compliance Platform — the infrastructure and operational capabilities for Ramp’s government environments and compliance needs: secure access, deployment paths, environment validation, and technical controls that let product teams deliver reliably within regulatory and compliance requirements.

jobs.description:
Director of Engineering - Databricks Commercialization & Marketplace 

P-1630

About the role

Every product Databricks ships has to be priced, contracted, rated and billed before it can earn a dollar. The Money organization builds the systems that make this happen, at hyperscaler scale and across every major cloud. We built the world's only cross-cloud integrated rating engine in-house, and it now rates billions of dollars in revenue. Our next goal is bigger: a fully automated, zero-touch order-to-cash flow where the platform is the source of truth for accounts, contracts and subscriptions, and Month End Close needs little or no human intervention.

As Director of Engineering, you will lead the engineering organization that owns this commercial engine from start to finish. You will set the product and technology strategy for how Databricks makes money. You will be the engineering voice Finance, Product and GTM leaders turn to for strategic decisions. You will also build the leadership bench that lets the organization keep scaling.

Speed is critical. Databricks keeps inventing new ways to sell: commit and pay-as-you-go, marketplaces, conditional benefits, strategic partnerships and new clouds and regions. The commerce engine either makes each of these fast and safe to launch, or it becomes the bottleneck. You will make sure it is the former.

What you'll own

The org covers six commercial domains:

  • Pricing configuration: SKUs, multipliers, price-change processes, deal desk and discounting
  • Orders and contracts: from negotiated quote to order to signed customer contract
  • Subscriptions: commit, pay-as-you-go and proof-of-concept subscriptions, plus how contracts are tied to payment methods
  • Rating: applying each customer's negotiated price, discounts and conditional benefits to ingested usage to compute the bill
  • Billing: commit drawdown, invoicing, Month End Close and related financial processes
  • Marketplace: third-party data and solutions, available seamlessly to Databricks customers

The impact you'll have

  • Set and communicate the vision. Write the multi-year product and technology strategy for the commerce engine, toward a zero-touch order-to-cash flow and a next-generation billing architecture. Present it clearly to executives, Finance and Product leaders, so that strategy and architecture decisions come to you by default.
  • Own business outcomes across orgs, not just your team's part. Revenue-critical programs routinely span 100+ people across Finance, Product, IT, Accounts and GTM. You will own the full outcome: dependency plans with clear owners, timelines, quality bars and escalation triggers, raised early in leadership forums so cross-org risks don't become executive surprises.
  • Make commercialization a platform capability. Build reusable building blocks (credits, commits, conditional benefits, marketplace and partner billing) so that new pricing models and routes to market ship in weeks, not quarters.
  • Treat foundations as seriously as features. Hold reliability, correctness, SOX and compliance readiness, security, cost visibility and operational load to the same standard as product launches. Billing errors should be structurally impossible, operational work should grow more slowly than revenue, and postmortems should actually lead to change.
  • Partner deeply with Business & Finance. Turn accounting, close and compliance requirements into engineering design. Keep improving the Month End Close timeline and audit readiness, and earn the trust of Technica

jobs.title: AI Automation Engineer
jobs.description:

We're hiring an AI Automation Engineer to build the next generation of IT automations to improve the employee experience at Databricks.

You'll be building production-grade AI agents and automation services that understand employee requests, retrieve enterprise context, reason across systems, invoke tools and APIs, and take action safely. The goal isn't to automate existing workflows the same way we've done it for the past decade. It's to reimagine how employees interact with IT through intelligent, contextual, and increasingly agentic experiences and to do it on Databricks.

What you will do

  • Build AI agents and automations: Design, deploy, and run AI agents that support all of our employees. The agents interpret natural-language requests, gather context, select tools, execute actions, and communicate outcomes.
  • Maintain MCP servers across our AI tools portfolio.
  • Build agentic workflows that decompose goals into steps, handle failures, pause for human approval as needed, and resume their workflows.
  • Ground agents in trusted internal knowledge (policies, runbooks, system documentation, SOPs, etc).
  • Turn high-volume support CUJs into self-service experiences: Identify repetitive, high-friction IT interactions and convert them into reliable AI automation experiences.
  • Instrument AI automations with logs, metrics, and feedback loops.
  • Design and implement AI automations with identity governance, tools RBAC, human-in-the-loop approvals where applicable, audit trails, and failure handling.
  • Create shared automation infrastructure (credential vaults, event ingestion, scheduling, approval workflows, cache/state stores) that other teams can build on.
  • Work with IT Support, Employee Experience, Security, IAM, Infrastructure, and Engineering to identify automation opportunities and take solutions from prototype to production.
  • Write and maintain high-quality technical/engineering documentation that clearly communicates system designs, operational procedures, and architectural decisions.

What we are looking for

  • Proficiency in Python or Go [3yrs].
  • Experience with Git-based development, automated testing, and CI/CD.
  • Strong experience with REST APIs, OAuth2/authentication frameworks, event-driven integrations, and enterprise system integrations.
  • Shipped production LLM-powered applications or AI agents.
  • Experience with agent patterns: tool/function calling, multi-step workflows, context management, RAG, structured outputs, and plan decomposition.

  • Experience integrating IT platforms: Okta/Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Jira, Slack, Jamf, GitHub, Workd
