jobs.title: Regional Director, Forward Deployed Engineering - Financial Services
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

Our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) embed with customer engineering teams to build production-grade AI coding workflows and leave behind engineering practices that customers can sustain. As Regional Director, you will lead the team serving banks, insurers, asset managers, and other financial institutions globally, owning the quality of engagements from technical discovery through delivery and handoff. Success means production workflows that customers adopt, measurable progress against agreed outcomes, and customer engineers able to operate and sustain the work after handoff.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Build and lead a team of Forward Deployed Engineers and Strategists, reporting to the Global Head of FDE. Own hiring, coaching, performance management, staffing, and career development, and hold the team to a clear bar for engineering quality and delivery.

 - Own technical scoping: work backwards from customer outcomes, run discovery and architecture reviews, and turn ambiguous problems into time-boxed engagements with defined scope, acceptance criteria, milestones, risks, and change control.

 - Validate integration, infrastructure, and data constraints early, including retention, entitlements, PII, and other sensitive customer-data requirements, and hold the production engineering bar across engagements: code and architecture review, secure integration, evaluation of model behavior and workflow quality, observability, and failure handling.

 - Own delivery through deployment and operational handoff, making sure customer teams have the documentation, operating practices, and ownership to sustain the work, and partner with Sales and Legal so proposals, statements of work, and commitments match technical feasibility and team capacity.

 - Serve as technical owner and executive sponsor on the highest-priority engagements, guiding customers through procurement, third-party risk, security, compliance, and model-risk reviews, and working across engineering, business, and risk stakeholders to resolve tradeoffs.

 - Run a detailed feedback loop with Product and Engineering, turning recurring constraints and successful implementations into product feedback, reusable delivery patterns, and reference architectures, and enable GSI and consulting partners to the same standards as the in-house team.




BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Experience directly managing engineers who build and ship production software, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and setting technical standards.

 - Professional software development experience in Python, JavaScript, or TypeScript, with the judgment to review code, assess architectures, and diagnose integration and production issues.

 - Experience building, deploying, and operating AI-powered workflows in production, including evaluating model behavior, debugging failures, and establishing appropriate observability and security controls.




PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

 - A track record of owning technical engagements from discovery and scoping through production delivery, customer adoption, and operational handoff.

 - Experience delivering inside regulated enterprises and serving as the technical ow

Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. jobs.title: Development Platform Partner Manager
jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Deepgram is bringing the world’s most natural interface, voice, to the technology we use every day. Our speech models and real-time infrastructure power AI systems that keep up with the way people actually speak. More than 5,000 organizations run conversational voice AI on Deepgram in production, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box.



The Deepgram Voice Agent Platform brings together speech-to-text, text-to-speech and speech-to-speech, with voice-native foundation models available through cloud APIs or self-hosted and on-premises deployments. Built for accuracy, low latency and cost efficiency, Deepgram makes high-quality voice experiences practical to build and run at scale. More than 650,000 developers have used Deepgram to process more than 200,000 years of audio. Every day, more of the world’s conversations with AI run on our models.




OPERATING PRINCIPLES

Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:

 1. Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.

 2. Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.

 3. Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.

 4. Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.

We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.




AI-FIRST BY DEFAULT

We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.

That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:

 - Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.

 - Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.

 - Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.

 - Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.

We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment.



Deepgram’s Partnerships team makes Deepgram the voice layer wherever businesses and developers build. As Dev Platform Partner Manager, you’d own our relationships with the platforms where the next wave of voice apps gets built, hosted and scaled: AI app builders, edge and inference clouds, and model routers. You’d also help grow the Deepgram Marketplace, our catalog of complementary voice AI services. There are a few live relationships and a lot of white space. You’d decide what gets built in it, and then build it.

What You Will Do:

 - Make Deepgram the default or recommended voice provider inside our highest-priority dev platforms, with commercial terms that hold up, working with Finance and Legal

 - Build and keep re-ranking a focused partner portfolio, putting time where developer reach, voice AI fit and revenue potential are highest

 - Shorten the path from a developer’s first click to paid usage by shipping integrations, templates, starter apps and docs with DevRel, Product and partner teams

 - Turn usage on partner platforms into Deepgram customers by spotting builders who are scaling and bringing Sales in at the right moment

 - Grow partner-sourced and influenced revenue, usage and attach, and be the source of truth on how the ecosystem is performing

 - Bring partner and developer insight back to Product so it shapes our SDKs, integra

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About Beneficial Deployments 

Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences — focusing on raising the floor for those who need it most.

About the Role

We're looking for an Applied AI Architect to join Beneficial Deployments, focused on helping public health, global health and humanitarian organizations get real value from Claude. You'll be the technical lead for partners such as public health agencies and ministries of health, the institutes and NGOs that support them, and humanitarian organizations working in crisis settings. You'll help them find where Claude makes a real difference, from disease surveillance and outbreak response to health data, communications and program delivery, design solutions that fit their data, privacy and procurement rules, and turn early pilots into lasting deployments. What works for one partner becomes something the whole field can use.

 

Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary technical advisor to a portfolio of health partners from discovery through deployment, turning their priorities into scoped use cases with clear measures of success.

  • Design and demo solutions with Claude, the API, Claude Science and Claude Code across surveillance, outbreak response, data analysis and public communications.

  • Guide partners through security review, data governance and procurement, from national agencies to field operations.

  • Run workshops, trainings and tabletop exercises that build AI fluency across partner teams.

  • Build reusable assets (reference designs, connectors, prompt and eval templates) so one partner's work helps the next.

  • Spot patterns across partners, bring field insight back to Product and Research, and help partners measure what changed.

  • Travel to partner sites for workshops, technical deep dives and relationship building.

 

You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have

  • 3+ years in customer-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, sales engineering, forward-deployed engineering or technical consulting.

  • Experience working with public health agencies, ministries of health, global health or humanitarian organizations, or similarly complex public institutions, including how they buy, adopt, and govern technology.

  • A track record of making technology stick inside slow-moving organizations with many stakeholders.

  • Hands-on experience building with LLM APIs: you can prototype a working demo. You don't need to write production code.

  • Clear written and spoken communication across a broad audience. The ability to explain technical tradeoffs to epidemiologists, program leads, field teams and executives.

  • Patience with long buying cycles, a knack for knowing how to make them go smoothly, and real care for public benefit.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity: you bring clarity to fuzzy problems, wear multiple hats and do whatever it takes to further the mission.

  • Bonus if you've worked on disease surveillance, outbreak response, health information systems or emergency operations.

jobs.title: Technical Marketing Engineer
jobs.description:
About The Role

Most of what makes Together AI so valuable for customers is invisible from the outside. Optimizing kernels, scheduling, quantization, speculative decoding, and more create an industry-leading platform for inference and post-training at scale. As a technical marketing engineer, you are the conduit between the engineering and research work and the developers who should know about it. You go deep with product, engineering, research, and CX to learn the platform at the level of nuanced technical detail, then decide which details matter to an AI builder and build content that makes them care.

This is a creator role. You are a technical storyteller. You'll produce social-native posts, technical blogs, performance benchmarks, demo and explainer videos, and thought leadership, all aimed at one outcome: building Together’s credibility with developers. You'll also own our technical communities on X, YouTube, Discord, Linkedin and the engagement metrics for developer content company-wide, including amplifying the work of engineers and researchers who publish under their own names.

Responsibilities

External

  • Partner with product, engineering, DevRel, research, and CX to learn new capabilities in technical depth, then extract the most meaningful aspects for a developer audience.
  • Create the content strategy based on deep understanding of our company’s differentiation and marries that with an understanding of the content that would resonate.
  • Build technical content across formats: blogs, videos, benchmark reports, podcasts, and short-form posts that drive engagement with developers and preference for Together.
  • Monitor real-time news and announcements related to AI infrastructure and lead timely responses working with product and engineering
  • Replies to social media comments, bringing expert understanding of the technology
  • Own Together's presence in technical communities, primarily X, Discord, LinkedIn, and Youtube. Track engagement metrics, what lands, what doesn't, and adjust.
  • Drive amplification of engineering and research work across social channels.
  • Be the heartbeat of the Together AI technical community - understanding the developers and researchers who follow us and enabling them to be successful
  • Experiment and test new ideas to see what resonates with the community
  • While the role involved mainly online engagement (80%), there is an aspect of translating their deep understanding to deliver highly engaging in-person meet ups and events (20%) in collaboration with Events/ DevRel teams

Internal

  • Be the bridge between research and engineering with the field team
  • Deploy models, benchmark new capabilities (e.g. the compiler, speculative decoding) across models and workloads, and turn results into practical field guidance: when to use it, when not to, and what to expect.
  • Enable SAs and FDEs on every launch. Create technical briefs and run sessions covering how it works, where it sits in the inference serving stack, how to deploy it for customers
  • Go to implementation depth for FDEs: which workload and model shapes a capability fits, how to configure it, and how to implement it.

We are an AI-first company. This means you approach your work with a growth mindset and find ways to leverage AI to help make faster, smarter decisions that will 10X your impact at Box.

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's legal team operates at the frontier of some of the most consequential legal and regulatory questions of our time — from landmark copyright matters to first-of-their-kind AI regulatory frameworks emerging across dozens of jurisdictions simultaneously. As we scale, the volume and complexity of our discovery and information governance obligations are growing rapidly.

We are looking for a Discovery Technical Operations Specialist to join our Litigation and Regulatory team and help build out Anthropic's discovery operations from the ground up, support active matters, and help drive information governance maturation. This is a unique opportunity to be a part of a critical function at one of the most closely watched companies in the world. You will work hand-in-hand with our discovery leads, litigation and regulatory counsel, outside counsel, discovery vendors, and cross-functional partners such as Security and IT to manage retention, preservation, collection, and production of electronically stored information (ESI) across active matters. Beyond matter-level support and programmatic development of discovery systems and processes, you will also help execute the development of Anthropic's broader information governance program, including data classification standards and defensible disposal practices that keep pace with a rapidly scaling AI company's evolving data landscape.

The right person for this role will be equal parts technical operator and operational project manager.

Key responsibilities

  • Build and operate discovery operations across the full EDRM lifecycle (preservation, collection, processing, hosting, review, and production including for novel and AI-specific data types)

  • Support the operational design and execution of the legal hold program including custodian identification workflows, hold issuance and tracking, periodic re-notification, custodian acknowledgments, and defensible release

  • Support and improve the discovery technology stack including RelativityOne, in-place preservation and collection tooling across Slack, Google Workspace, and internal systems, and supporting analytics and review platforms including configuration, access controls, templates, and reusable workspaces

  • Partner with discovery team, in-house counsel, outside counsel, vendors, and internal technical teams; coordinate matter execution, status, and escalations

  • Partner with Security, IT, and product engineering to support Anthropic's data landscape, instrument new data sources for hold and collection, and ensure each ESI source has a governed retention, hold, and disposition path

  • Improve and support the operational layer of Anthropic's information governance program: retention schedule execution, classification rollout, defensible disposition workflows, and data-inventory maintenance in close partnership with the Discovery Lead and information governance stakeholders

  • Integrate AI and automation into the EDRM lifecycle: generative-AI-assisted review, advanced analytics, custom Relativity applications, and agentic workflow automation for intake, hold tracking, status reporting, and internal documentation

  • Support active litigation, government investigations, and regulatory inquiries as the operational counterpart on the matter team coordinating workstreams, managing vendor execution, and surfacing operational risk and cost trade-offs to counsel

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Index Engineer, Search Crawler)
jobs.description:
AI answers are only as trustworthy as the information behind them. Perplexity grounds its answers in fresh, real-world sources, and the index is what makes that possible. We're looking for an engineer to work on the indexing and data processing layer of Perplexity's Search Crawler. You'll build systems that ingest, process, and organize large volumes of crawled content into efficient, queryable structures, working primarily on offline and nearline pipelines that keep data fresh, complete, and accessible to downstream retrieval. Throughput, scalability, and correctness are critical across datasets that change continuously.



Responsibilities 

 - Design, implement, and operate large-scale indexing systems and data pipelines at the core of Perplexity's search infrastructure.

 - Develop and optimize indexing strategies that balance performance, freshness, and resource efficiency.

 - Work on storage formats, compaction, and update mechanisms that keep data accessible and current.

 - Keep pipelines reliable and predictable under high-throughput conditions. 

 - Build well-tested components with clear responsibilities and interface contracts that stay flexible as the system evolves.

 - Define and implement observability across offline and near line pipelines, including structured logs, metrics, and data quality signals.

 - Monitor throughput, resource usage, and cost, and drive optimisations as business needs change.

 - Partner with retrieval, ranking, and ML teams to make sure indexing outputs meet their requirements.

 - Enable safe experimentation on indexing strategies and processing logic through controlled rollouts and clearly defined quality signals.
   
   

Qualifications

 - 5+ years of experience building production backend or data infrastructure systems.

 - Strong programming experience in Go, C++, or Rust.

 - Experience with high-throughput data processing systems and very large datasets.

 - Experience building or operating databases, storage systems, data planes, or indexing pipelines.

 - Strong understanding of distributed systems, fault tolerance, consistency, and scalability.

 - Experience running production systems and handling operational incidents.

 - A systems-thinking mindset and the ability to reason about end-to-end data flows.

jobs.title: Senior/Staff System Research Engineer – LLM Inference Optimization
jobs.description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.
We are looking for talented systems developers and researchers to join the Snowflake AI Research team and advance the state of the art in LLM inference systems and optimization.

Our mission is to build the next generation of high-performance and intelligent inference systems. We optimize not only how fast and efficiently models run, but also how quickly inference systems can adapt to new models, architectures, hardware, and workloads.

Our work spans the full inference stack—from distributed serving and runtime systems to GPU kernels and model-system co-design. We explore techniques such as adaptive parallelism, speculative and parallel decoding, disaggregated inference, scheduling and batching, KV-cache optimization, model swapping, quantization, and GPU kernel optimization to push the frontier of latency, throughput, scalability, and cost.

Beyond optimizing individual models, we are building intelligent and adaptive inference systems that can automate performance optimization—rapidly profiling new models and workloads, identifying bottlenecks, selecting effective execution strategies, and adapting system configurations with minimal manual tuning. We embrace AI-native engineering, using AI not only as the workload we optimize, but also as a tool to accelerate system development, experimentation, debugging, optimization, and adaptation to new models. Our goal is to accelerate both the speed of inference and the agility of inference development.

This is an exciting opportunity to collaborate with a world-class team, including founding members of DeepSpeed, vLLM, and TensorFlow. Together, we will push the boundaries of AI systems and bring cutting-edge research into production-scale AI.

Responsibilities
• Design and develop high-performance LLM inference systems, spanning distributed serving, runtime systems, GPU execution, and performance-critical kernels.

• Develop novel techniques to improve inference latency, generation speed, throughput, memory efficiency, scalability, and cost.

• Explore advanced inference techniques including speculative and parallel decoding, prefill/decode disaggregation, adaptive parallelism, continuous batching and scheduling, KV-cache management, quantization, and communication optimization.

• Develop adaptive and intelligent inference systems that automatically optimize execution for new model architectures, hardware platforms, workload characteristics, and deployment environments.

• Apply AI-driven and AI-native approaches to systems engineering, including automated profiling, bottleneck identification, configuration search, code generation, experimentation, runtime strategy selection, debugging, and performance tuning.

• Independently identify high-impact performance and systems problems, formulate hypotheses, prototype solutions, and drive promising ideas from research through production.

• Design distributed inference strategies across GPUs and nodes, including tensor, sequence, pipeline, data, and expert parallelism.

• Develop efficient approaches for multi-model serving, dynamic resource management, model loading and swapping, and workload-aware scheduling.

• Analyze and optimize GPU kernels and operators for attention, MoE, communication, and other performance-critical model components.

jobs.title: Agent Deployment Engineer
jobs.description:
About Decagon

Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences.

Our technology enables industry-defining enterprises like Avis Budget Group, Block’s Cash App and Square, Chime, Oura Health, and Hunter Douglas to deploy AI agents that power personalized, deeply satisfying interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel.

We’re building a future where customer experiences are being redefined from support tickets and hold music to faster resolutions, richer conversations, and deeper relationships. We’re proud to be backed by world-class investors who share that vision, including a16z, Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, and Index Ventures, along with many others.

We’re an in-office company, driven by a shared commitment to excellence and velocity. Our values — Just Get It Done, Invent What Customers Want, Winner’s Mindset, and The Polymath Principle — shape how we work and grow as a team.



About the Team

Over the past few years, development of LLMs has evolved at a rapid pace. It’s not enough for our customers to just “set it and forget it” when it comes to AI software. Truly successful AI Agents require hands-on execution, rigorous iteration, and deep technical delivery to reach enterprise-grade performance.

We’re creating an Agent Deployment Engineering Org: a specialized technical delivery team responsible for end-to-end execution of AI agent builds. Agent Deployment Engineers own the hands-on work required to deliver best-in-class agents—writing and configuring key components, validating integrations, and ensuring agents perform reliably at scale. This team brings greater specialization and focus to build quality. Agent Deployment Engineers are technical and customer-facing: you’ll interface with senior technical stakeholders on the customer side while also going deep on agent configuration and build execution.



About the Role

As an Agent Deployment Engineer, you will be responsible for end-to-end execution of AI agent builds for strategic customers. This is a highly technical delivery role where you will own the implementation work required to launch and scale enterprise-quality agents—partnering with customers and internal teams to define success, translate requirements into build plans, and deliver agents that meaningfully impact the customer’s business.

You’ll work closely with Agent PMs, Agent Success, Engineering, and GTM teams to create tight feedback loops: executing builds, surfacing gaps, and influencing the evolution of Decagon’s agent-building platform based on real customer needs. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in fast-moving environments, enjoys shipping customer-facing technical work, and can balance hands-on execution with structured thinking.



In this role, you will

 - Own end-to-end architecture and execution of AI agent builds for enterprise customers, from systems design and initial scoping through implementation, evaluation, and production deployment.

 - Design and engineer the core agentic logic governing agent behavior, applying engineering principles to optimize quality, reliability, and correctness across non-deterministic model outputs.

 - Engineer and validate layered guardrails and supervisory controls to ensure safe, compliant, and predictable agent performance across real-world scenarios.

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

Autonomy in the real world is never fully hands-off. Our machines work alongside expert operators who support them from anywhere, and the tools those operators use are a core part of the product.  - Partner closely with autonomy, backend, and infrastructure engineers to define how people and machines work together, and what the system needs from each

WHAT YOU BRING

Perplexity is growing fast, and every new employee, laptop, SaaS app and integration expands what we have to protect. We want enterprise security that's strong by default, mostly automated, and invisible to people doing their jobs.



We're looking for an Enterprise Security Engineer to own the security of how Perplexity works internally: our identities, devices, SaaS applications and corporate access.  - Build access governance that scales: just-in-time and request-based access, regular access reviews, and joiner/mover/leaver automation that removes access promptly and reliably.

 - Partner with IT, People, Legal and GRC on new tools and vendors, security reviews, and evidence for compliance programs.

 - 4+ years in security engineering, with significant time on corporate or enterprise security, identity, or endpoint security.

 - Experience securing SaaS environments such as Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, Slack, and developer tools, including OAuth and third-party app risk.

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

The Data Infrastructure team at Cohere is responsible for the storage and data movement layer underlying every model training run. We're building the unified storage layer that feeds our training workloads at petabyte scale. In this role, you would have the opportunity to architect and lead the design of this system from the ground up, serving petabytes of training data and model checkpoints fast enough to keep thousands of GPUs busy across several training clusters. You'd be a key contributor, leading the effort to solve a problem few teams have tackled at this scale.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Design, architect, and operate the distributed storage system that feeds model training and evaluation, driving the technical vision from concept through production.

 - Lead and own the deployment of this system across multiple Kubernetes clusters at petabyte scale, setting standards and best practices for the organization.

 - Collaborate with researchers and training-infra teams to define how jobs read and write data, translating those patterns into throughput, latency, and durability requirements that shape the platform's roadmap.

 - Navigate the networking, I/O, and consistency challenges of moving large datasets and checkpoints across regions and backends, with GPU idle time and time-to-insight as the key metrics of success — and drive the solutions that improve them.


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE:

 - Strong storage fundamentals, including replication, consistency, caching, and data lifecycle management, with demonstrated architecture and design experience.

 - Strong coding ability in Python and Go, with the ability to lead implementations and mentor others in either language, and the willingness to contribute to the other.

 - Proven experience running stateful systems on Kubernetes, including Persistent Volumes, CSI drivers, and StatefulSets, with the capacity to design and execute operational strategies.

 - Hands-on experience with cloud object storage such as S3 as well as POSIX-style filesystems.

You'll own the infrastructure that runs our deploy anywhere platform — from Kubernetes clusters serving ML inference at scale to the CI/CD pipelines, IaC, and observability stack that keep it all reliable. This is a hands-on role: you'll write Helm charts and Terraform one day, debug a Kafka consumer lag issue the next, and ship a backend service feature the day after. jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer - Alternative Access
jobs.description:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.
Plaid's Connectivity team builds and operates the network that powers open finance, connecting consumers' financial accounts to the apps and services they choose to use across thousands of institutions. Where an institution offers an API, we use it. Where one doesn't, we still need a dependable, secure way to honor a consumer's request to share their own data. The Alternative Access team owns that path: the client, network and reliability systems that make consumer-permissioned connections work when no API is available.
You will be the hands-on technical lead for alternative access. You will set its direction and build the systems yourself: browser- and mobile-based clients that act on the consumer's behalf, the network egress infrastructure those sessions run through, credential and session handling, and the measurement that tells us how well it all works.
Institutions' traffic controls often cannot distinguish a consumer-directed session from unwanted automation. You will study how real clients behave at the browser, device and network level, and make permissioned sessions faithful to that behavior so that consumers' connections stay reliable as institutions change.
You will turn today's approach into a platform that can be extended to new institutions in weeks, decide where to build versus buy, and partner closely with Legal, Policy, Security and Product so that every method we deploy is one we're confident in. This is a role with direct visibility to Plaid's leadership and a clear path to leading the area.
Responsibilities:
• You'll design, build and operate the production systems that let consumers share data from institutions without an API.

• You'll research how browsers, mobile apps and networks present themselves to institutions and keep permissioned sessions consistent with real client behavior.

• You'll build and run egress and proxy infrastructure, and evaluate routing approaches and vendors on effectiveness, cost and risk.

• You'll instrument success rate, breakage detection and time to repair, and drive staged rollouts with Product and Account Management.

• You'll write the design and risk documentation that lets leadership make deployment decisions, and bring Legal, Policy and Security in early.

• You'll mentor engineers and raise the technical bar across Connectivity through design reviews and hands-on work.

Qualifications:
• 6+ years of software engineering experience, including hands-on work building and operating systems that act on a user's behalf against third-party web or mobile applications at scale.

• Deep knowledge of browser internals and automation (Chromium, Chrome DevTools Protocol, Playwright or Puppeteer) or of mobile application internals and instrumentation.

• Experience-based understanding of traffic classification and fingerprinting (device, browser, TLS and network signals, behavioral signals).

• Experience designing and operating network egress and proxy infrastructure.

• Strong reliability instincts: you instrument what you build and find breakage before users do.

• Security-minded handling of credentials and sessions, and sound judgment about what to build, not just what is possible.

The MLOps Engineer builds and operates the platform and pipelines that take machine learning and AI models from development into reliable production use. jobs.title: Data Engineer Principal
jobs.description:
Domicile Information: This is a hybrid position in Plano, TX. Candidates residing within 50 miles of a FedEx campus will be required to work on-site at a FedEx location several times per week.
Business Summary
The Data Engineer Principal plays a pivotal role within FEC and provides dynamic leadership at the enterprise level. S/he is focused on fundamentally creating and driving engineering innovation within FEC, helping to define and build the FEC organization and overseeing the delivery of key business initiatives. S/he acts as a “universal translator” between IT, business, software engineers and data scientists, collaborating with these multi-disciplinary teams. The Data Engineer Principal will champion the creation and adherence of technical standards for data engineering, including the selection and refinement of foundational technical components. S/he will work on those aspects of the FEC platform that govern the ingestion, transformation, and pipelining of data assets, both to end users within FedEx and into data products and services that may be externally facing. Day-to-day, s/he will be deeply involved in code reviews, large scale deployments and general oversight. S/he will also mentor junior engineers to support the continued up-skilling of the Data Engineering team.
Essential Functions
• Define and evangelize the enterprise data platform architecture: lakehouse/warehouse patterns, ingestion/topology, storage tiers, data meshes, service boundaries, and governance guardrails.
• Design and build scalable batch and streaming data pipelines: CDC, bulk ingestion, event-driven streams, and real-time processing using technologies such as Kafka/Pub/Sub, Spark/Dataproc, Dataflow/Beam, Flink, or similar.
• Lead data modeling and schema strategy: canonical models, dimensional models, normalized/denormalized schemas, partitioning, clustering, and time-series best practices to maximize performance and cost-efficiency.
• Architect and implement ETL/ELT frameworks and orchestration: Airflow/Composer, Prefect, Dagster, Glue workflows, and robust dependency, retry, backfill and SLA handling.
• Design data storage and query platforms at scale: object storage, columnar warehouses (BigQuery/Redshift/Snowflake/Synapse), OLAP engines, and caching layers; define retention, compaction, and lifecycle policies.
• Build and maintain metadata, catalog, lineage and discovery capabilities: integrate Data Catalog/Atlas/Alation and automated lineage capture to support governance and self-serve analytics.
• Implement data quality, validation and observability: schema checks, unit tests, Great Expectations/Deequ checks, anomaly detection, SLIs/SLOs for data freshness, completeness and accuracy, and end-to-end monitoring and alerting.
• Drive security and compliance controls for data: fine-grained access controls (IAM, RBAC, ABAC), encryption (KMS/CMEK), tokenization/de-identification, PII discovery, VPC/private connectivity for data flows, and audit logging.
• Build reproducible infrastructure and platform modules for data workloads: Terraform/CloudFormation/Deployment Manager, container images, cluster templates, autoscaling, and policy-as-code for platform consistency.
• Optimize cost and performance of data workloads: query performance tuning, storage format choices (Parquet/ORC/Avro), compaction, caching, CUD or reserved capacity planning, and FinOps for analytics.
• Lead migrations and modernization efforts: lift-and-shift and re-architecture of on-prem or cross-cloud ETL and warehouses to modern cloud data platforms; own cutover, rollback, validation of RTO/RPO and performance targets.
• Enable ML/BI consumption: design feature stores, data marts, model inputs pipelines, and publishing patterns to support analytics, BI, and ML lifecycle teams.
• Establish CI/CD and dataops practices: testing (unit/integration/regression), artifact promotion, data pipeline deployments, schema evolution strategies, and GitOps for data infrastructure and pipeline

Cogniify is hiring an MLOps Engineer with 3 to 6 years of experience to run and scale our AI and machine learning systems. You will deploy open-source language models on GPU clusters, build the CI/CD pipelines that test and secure our code, and keep our AI applications fast and reliable.

You will work with software engineers, data scientists and product managers, and you will own features from the first idea to production.

Core skills for this role include MLOps, DevOps, Python, asyncio, Kubernetes, Ray, Slurm, GPU inference, vLLM, SGLang, LangChain, Hugging Face, GitLab CI/CD, DevSecOps, vulnerability scanning, PyTest and LLM evaluation.

• Monitor model and service performance in production, and track speed, cost and errors.
• Write clean, asynchronous Python for AI applications and agents, using simple designs that are easy to test and change.
• Prompt-tune models and agents, and build an easy way to compare models and swap one for another without rewriting the application.
• Run model benchmarks, study the wrong outputs to find gaps, and build dashboards that explain the findings in plain language.
• Write automated tests with PyTest and mocking libraries, and raise test coverage for both regular code and AI outputs that change from run to run.
• Take features from idea to production, make sound design choices, and keep clear notes on how things work.
• Keep Git history tidy with rebase and signed commits, and mirror code between internal and public repositories when needed.

What We Are Looking For

• 3 to 6 years of professional experience in MLOps, DevOps or software engineering, with at least 3 years of production Python, including asynchronous code with asyncio.
• Hands-on experience deploying, monitoring and scaling models or AI services in production on at least one of Kubernetes, Ray or Slurm.
• Working knowledge of GitLab CI/CD, including automated test jobs and vulnerability scanning on merge requests.
• Good understanding of GPU memory use and tuning for fast, low-latency AI inference.
• Hands-on experience with at least two of LangChain, Hugging Face libraries, vLLM and SGLang.
• Experience with prompt engineering, and with running structured LLM evaluations and benchmarks.
• Good data analysis skills in Python with pandas, NumPy or similar, and the ability to explain results clearly to both technical and non-technical people.
• Strong command of PyTest and mocking libraries, and experience writing tests for AI workloads.
• Good Git skills, including rebase workflows, commit signing and repository mirroring.
• A BS or higher in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
• Links to accepted pull requests, resolved issues or documentation you wrote in public AI repositories such as LangChain, Hugging Face, vLLM or SGLang are a big plus.
• A short write-up or repository link for an AI agent or multi-agent system you built, with accuracy numbers from your own benchmarks or gap analysis, is a plus.
• A GitLab or GitHub pipeline you designed to fix a testing, automation or security scanning problem is a plus.

jobs.description: At Boston Dynamics, our mission is to deliver the world’s most capable robots. Behind every robot is a lot of software, and on the Central Software (CSW) team, we build the “software factory” that gets it from a developer’s laptop to robots, desktops, and the cloud. We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer to take the next big leap in how fast and reliably many hundreds of engineers can build and test. Our monorepo spans C++, Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript, and Java/Kotlin, and targets embedded hardware, simulation, machine learning, and cloud services. That means build and test problems you won’t find at a typical web company: cross-compiling for robot hardware, large binary artifacts, and testing that has to bridge simulation and real machines. You’ll make an impact by: Owning the rollout of remote build execution across our monorepo, from proof of concept to production use by every developer. Teaming up with CSW leadership and peers to turn priorities into well-scoped, well-executed, and well-coordinated work. Improving build and test performance by profiling builds, raising cache hit rates, and eliminating non-determinism. Root-causing and fixing build breaks, flaky tests, and speed regressions. Modernizing our build, from migrating to current Bazel rulesets to using the dependency graph to generate SBOMs. Seeing everything through, from implementation and testing to deployment, documentation, and ongoing operations. Becoming one of the go-to Bazel experts on the team, staying current with the Bazel ecosystem and sharing what you learn through docs, code review, and helping teammates. Working in our agile process and communicating progress regularly. What we’re looking for: 5+ years as a software engineer working in large, cross-platform codebases. 3+ years of hands-on Bazel experience in a large codebase, including writing Starlark rules and debugging cache misses. A solid grasp of Bazel internals: configurations, toolchain resolution, and the action graph. Experience with remote execution and caching (e.g., EngFlow, BuildBuddy, Buildbarn, Buildfarm, NativeLink), or a track record that shows you could ramp up quickly. Proficiency in at least one general-purpose language such as Python, Go, Java, or C++. A talent for diagnosing and fixing hard bugs. A bachelor’s degree in a technical field (e.g., Engineering, Computer Science) or equivalent experience. Bonus points: Experience with embedded or robotics toolchains. Contributions to Bazel or open source rulesets. Experience structuring and completing large build migrations or upgrades. Experience with software supply chain tooling (SBOMs, provenance, dependency scanning). Experience operating remote execution infrastructure on Kubernetes. Familiarity with CI systems such as Jenkins, BuildKite, or GitLab. Help scale and optimize the software infrastructure driving Boston Dynamics' next generation of robotics! We are interested in all qualified candidates eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas for this position. The base pay range for this position is between $130,000 to $190,000 annually. Base pay will depend on multiple individualized factors including, but not limited to internal equity, job related knowledge, skills and experience. This range represents a good faith estimate of compensation at the time of posting. Boston Dynamics offers a generous Benefits package including medical, dental vision, 401(k), paid time off and an annual bonus structure. Additional details regarding these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer for employment. We are growing rapidly, building a commercial company that delivers cutting edge technology and solutions to our customers from industrial applications to logistics and warehouse solutions.

• You're not babysitting a legacy platform - you'll build at the frontier of AI, healthcare, and revenue intelligence.

• Join a leadership team with deep industry and technology experience.

• Help solve a $150B+ healthcare problem in a truly novel way.

• Make it production-grade: latency and cost budgets, fallbacks, observability, and a clear trail of why the system made each decision.

• Keep PHI safe inside every LLM workflow.

• Test new models fast and adopt only what the evals prove is better.

Qualifications

• 8+ years of engineering, including 3+ years shipping NLP or LLM systems to production.

• A strong AI, ML, and NLP foundation. An MSc or PhD in AI, ML, or NLP is a strong plus - shipped work counts just as much.

• Production RAG experience - retrieval quality, search and vector stores, hallucination defenses.

• Agentic systems experience - multi-step reasoning, tool use, and knowing when a plain workflow beats an agent.

• A real evaluation practice - eval datasets, LLM-as-judge calibrated against human review, and regression testing.

• Deep hands-on experience with frontier LLM APIs - prompting, structured outputs, long context, and cost control.

• Strong Python and the engineering discipline to put models behind clean, reliable services.

• You already build with AI coding agents every day and can show us how you direct them and review what they produce.

• Healthcare or clinical NLP experience is a plus.

• Comfort in startup environments - you move fast, take ownership, make decisions, and don't wait around for permission. Former founders and early-stage startup engineers are a strong plus.

• Claude, GPT, embeddings, rerankers, function calling, MCP.

• PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face, OCR and document parsing.

Your work will span model internals, quantization and model compression, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, inference engines, serving architecture, and benchmarking to improve latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, and cost per token while preserving model quality and reliability.

You will work with kernel and platform engineers to investigate serving problems, compare configurations, and resolve performance and quality regressions. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's go-to-market teams are scaling quickly, and the decisions they make, from who to sell to and how to cover them to where to invest next, are only as good as the intelligence and infrastructure underneath them. As a Data Engineer on the GTM Systems data foundations team, you'll help build that layer: the data products that give sellers, operators, and analysts a rich, current, and trusted picture of the market, and the engineering rigor that lets our GTM systems run reliably as the business grows.

This is an engineering role that goes beyond pipelines. You'll treat GTM data as a product and a platform: built once, kept current, and available wherever people work. Alongside the build, you'll help shape what the data means: how attributes are defined, which sources are trusted, and how the business puts them to use. The role sits at the intersection of the sales organization, the data organization, and the systems that data flows through. You'll partner closely with Sales Strategy and Operations, Finance, Data Science, and the central data engineering team.

Key responsibilities

  • Bring disparate internal and external sources together: orchestrate, model, and normalize first-party product and revenue data alongside third-party data into one usable understanding of the company landscape

  • Build and maintain identity and entity resolution, so every source attaches to one trusted record for each company and the relationships between companies are clear

  • Help build the canonical layer where key attributes are defined once and mean the same thing everywhere, with clear sourcing logic, provenance, and freshness

  • Turn data into intelligence: scores, signals, and AI-generated attributes that help GTM teams prioritize and act, held to the same quality bar as any other source

  • Deliver that intelligence to the surfaces where teams work, including the CRM, and bring production discipline to how data moves through those systems

  • Operate what you build as a living system, with observability, data quality, cost, security, and access controls designed in, so problems surface before the field sees them

  • Make the platform easy for other teams to build on, so work is contributed once and not rebuilt in silos

Minimum qualifications

  • Experience as a data engineer or analytics engineer building and operating production pipelines and data models

  • Strong SQL and Python, and experience with modern transformation and orchestration tooling on a cloud data warehouse

  • Experience making messy data from many sources usable, including record matching, deduplication, and reconciling conflicting values

  • Familiarity with go-to-market data and the CRM systems it flows through

  • Judgment beyond the pipeline: weighing data sources, shaping definitions with business partners, and making calls on data quality

  • Clear written and verbal communication with technical and non-technical partners

  • Regular hands-on use of AI tools in your engineering work

Preferred qualifications

jobs.description:
Your Job
The Senior LLM Engineer will fine-tune and deploy LLMs on Azure OpenAI / Azure AI Foundry to power generative AI capabilities within our engineering design platform, translating natural-language design intent into structured, engineering-valid outputs.

Our Team
Established in 1938, Molex delivers comprehensive electronic solutions for various markets, including data communications, telecommunications, consumer electronics, industrial, automotive, commercial vehicle, aerospace and defense, medical, and lighting. You'll join the platform team behind our Azure AI/ML engineering tools, working alongside ML engineers, data scientists, and MLOps teams to keep training and inference workloads reliable, secure, and cost-efficient.

What You Will Do

• Fine-tune foundation models (LoRA/QLoRA, RLHF/DPO, instruction tuning) for domain-specific tasks and terminology.

• Build agentic and tool-use workflows that connect the LLM to internal engineering tools and data sources.

• Design evaluation harnesses for factuality and accuracy; own hallucination and safety guardrails.

• Build RAG pipelines (Azure AI Search) and structured tool-use/function-calling systems on top of fine-tuned Azure OpenAI models.

• Deploy and optimize inference (quantization, KV-cache, vLLM/TensorRT-LLM) on Azure Kubernetes Service for cost-efficient serving.

Who You Are (Basic Qualifications)

• 8+ years overall ML/AI engineering experience, with deep hands-on LLM/foundation model work — not just calling APIs.

• Demonstrated experience fine-tuning models (LoRA/QLoRA/PEFT, full fine-tuning, or pretraining at some scale).

• Practical experience with alignment techniques (RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, or instruction tuning).

• Strong Python and deep PyTorch proficiency; solid grasp of transformer architecture internals.

• Hands-on experience building RAG pipelines, embeddings/vector search, and agentic or tool-use LLM systems.

• Familiarity with Azure OpenAI / Azure AI Foundry or an equivalent cloud LLM platform.

What Will Put You Ahead

• Direct experience with Azure OpenAI Service and Azure AI Foundry for enterprise-scale deployment.

• Experience orchestrating LLM-driven code or structured-output generation for technical/engineering domains.

• Distributed training experience across multi-GPU/multi-node clusters (DeepSpeed, FSDP).

• Publications, blog posts, or open-source contributions in generative AI.
